protections: sanitizeFilter() neutralizes user-supplied selector objects by wrapping any value whose immediate keys start with '$' in $eq, recursing into $and/$or, and honouring the trustedSymbol escape hatch (lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:17-35).
When sanitizeFilter is in effect, server-side-JS operators must not reach MongoDB; lib/cast.js:91-102 accepts '$where' as a string/function and no sanitizer or cast check rejects it.

The sanitizeFilter setting must be effective on every documented route (per-query option, mongoose.set global, connect/connection option) and, when effective, must also disable implicit $in (lib/query.js:2295-2306, lib/query.js:4904-4915, lib/cast.js:376).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: sanitizeFilter is documented to wrap nested selector objects; a top-level $where is an operator the developer writes through Query#$where/Model.$where, and the docs tell users not to pass whole user objects as filters, so the key can be treated as trusted even though the pinned tree contains no rejection for it.
evidence: lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:23-26 — only $and/$or keys are handled; every other key falls through
lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28 — hasDollarKeys returns false for a string $where value, so nothing is wrapped
lib/cast.js:91-102 — $where is accepted as a string (and a function is stringified), with no sanitizeFilter check
lib/query.js:2304-2306 — sanitizeFilter() runs on the conditions before cast and leaves the $where key in place
lib/query.js:322-347 and lib/model.js:2223-2227 — $where is a documented developer-facing query operator, which supplies the dismissal

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the sanitizer already recurses into $and/$or and the cast layer already descends into $nor, so $nor looks covered; it is a rarely used operator and a report centred on $where invites a fix that adds a guard in the visited keys without adding $nor to the recursion list.
evidence: lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:23 — the recursion list contains only '$and' and '$or'
lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28 — $nor's value is an array, so hasDollarKeys inspects index keys ('0') and finds no '$', leaving every sub-filter untouched
lib/cast.js:65 — cast() does descend into $nor, so the unsanitized sub-filter survives cast and reaches the collection
test/helpers/query.sanitizeFilter.test.js:28-36 — the committed tests cover $and/$or only, matching the code's list

traps.reason_to_dismiss: sanitizeFilter is documented as a Mongoose/query option and the connect option is visibly stored on the connection, so a solver may assume the query path picks it up, or may not exercise the connect route at all because the report uses setOptions().

lib/query.js:2296-2297 — the query path reads this.model.db.options, not conn.config
lib/connection.js:61 and 181-190 — Connection#options starts null and is only populated by conn.set()
lib/connection.js:153-159 — Connection#get consults config first, showing config is a real store the query path bypasses
test/connection.test.js:1042-1045 — the connect option is asserted to land in config, confirming where it is stored
types/connection.d.ts:53-58 — ConnectOptions advertises sanitizeFilter

traps.reason_to_dismiss: implicit $in is ordinary Mongoose casting and the sanitizer itself does run for the global route, so the filter looks protected; nothing in a $where report points at array values or at Query.cast's option plumbing.

lib/query.js:4913-4915 — Query.cast builds opts.sanitizeFilter only from this._mongooseOptions
lib/cast.js:376 — implicit $in is allowed whenever opts.sanitizeFilter is not set

traps.reason_to_dismiss: sanitizeFilter is documented as a Query option and bulkWrite takes raw driver-style operation objects the application assembles, so its filters look out of scope; a solver may assume every filter passes through Query._castConditions.
evidence: lib/helpers/model/castBulkWrite.js:7-8 — only cast() and castUpdate() are imported; there is no sanitizeFilter dependency
lib/helpers/model/castBulkWrite.js:100-103 — updateOne filters are cast with { strict, upsert } only
lib/helpers/model/castBulkWrite.js:159-162 and 183-186 — updateMany and replaceOne filters are cast the same way

traps.reason_to_dismiss: the lone-$eq shortcut exists precisely so legitimate {$expr: {$eq: [...]}} queries keep working, so an object with a single $eq key reads as already-safe and its operands are never inspected; $function is an aggregation-expression operator rather than the $where selector a report names.
evidence: lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28-33 — a value whose only key is $eq is skipped entirely and its subtree is never visited
lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28 — $expr's {$eq: [...]} value hits that skip
lib/cast.js:103-104 — $expr is passed to cast$expr(), not rejected
lib/helpers/query/cast$expr.js:104-117 — only a fixed operator allow-list is walked; unknown expression keys such as $function are left untouched and never rejected

conflicts.what: A broad T1 fix that rejects every '$'-prefixed key (or wraps every operator object) would also close T6 but would collide with the must-keep-working lone-$eq $expr shape (lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28-33) and the trusted() bypass (:20-22); T1 has to stay narrow to $where while T6 needs operand inspection instead of wrapping.

The two fixes are conjunctive for the $where-under-$nor route: recursing into $nor (T2) does not reject a string-valued $where because hasDollarKeys is false (lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:28), and a $where guard (T1) never runs inside $nor because $nor is not in the recursion list (:23); implementing only the line a report names leaves the other half open.

fairness_risks: Rejecting $where under sanitizeFilter contradicts legitimate Query#$where / Model.$where use (lib/query.js:322-347, lib/model.js:2223-2227); the escape hatch has to remain mongoose.trusted() (lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:20-22, test/helpers/query.sanitizeFilter.test.js:18-26).

A rule that rejects or wraps every '$'-prefixed key would break legitimate developer-written $and/$or/$expr/$text queries; the sanitizer must keep its current $and/$or recursion and lone-$eq exemption (lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:23-33, test/helpers/query.sanitizeFilter.test.js:28-36).

Recursing into $nor changes behaviour for legitimate developer-written $nor filters in sanitizeFilter mode: nested operator objects become $eq-wrapped, exactly as $and/$or already are, so apps relying on the old pass-through need trusted().
T6's fix must preserve legitimate {$expr: {$eq: [...]}} queries; a blanket ban on operators inside $expr breaks aggregation-expression filters (lib/helpers/query/cast$expr.js:9, 104-117).

T4's implicit-$in rule must not disable implicit $in when sanitizeFilter is off; cast.js:376 already gates it on the option and test/query.test.js:3524-3536 expects a CastError only with sanitizeFilter enabled.

design.why: T1 and T2 are the actual A->B incomplete-fix pair: T1 is the $where guard the pinned 8.8.2 tree never had, and T2 is the $nor container that a guard placed in the sanitizer loop cannot reach, so the pair exercises two different judgements in the same function and a solver who implements only the line a report names fails one of them. T5 adds a parallel entry point (bulkWrite filters) with a strong 'not a Query' dismissal, and T6 adds the coupled-value judgement (keep the lone-$eq $expr exemption working while inspecting its operands) that is the MiMo failure mode. The four groups live in three files, carry four different dismissal arguments, and are all fixable in-repo with no dependency bump. Replacing T5/T6 with the connect-option plumbing group (T3/T4) would test the same feature but rests on a weaker security premise and on configuration-plumbing assertions rather than filter sanitization.

unverified: The pinned commit is the 8.8.2 release (package.json:4, CHANGELOG.md:1) and predates the CVE-2024-53900 fix, so the exact code site and shape of fix A cannot be read from this tree; that A rejects $where is inferred from the advisory refs supplied by the harness, not from pinned code.

B's exact route is inferred from GHSA-vg7j-7cwx-8wgw being the incomplete fix of CVE-2024-53900: no advisory text was available, so the $where-through-$nor shape is a hypothesis supported by the missing $nor recursion at lib/helpers/query/sanitizeFilter.js:23 rather than by quoted advisory text.
MongoDB-side acceptance was not executed: $where inside $nor, and $function inside $expr (T6), are assumed to be valid query expressions; if server-side scripting is disabled the T6 route is inert.

No report text or hidden-test text was available, so tier estimates assume a report that names $where and possibly $nor and do not account for wording that would make either surface trivially discoverable.
T3's claim that the connect/connect-option never sanitizes rests on static reading of lib/query.js:2296-2297 versus lib/drivers/node-mongodb-native/connection.js:263-266; no runtime probe was run.
T5's scope depends on whether the sanitizeFilter contract is meant to cover bulkWrite; lib/mongoose.js:235 says 'query filters', which is ambiguous for raw bulkWrite operations.

A's fix could in principle have been implemented in lib/cast.js rather than in sanitizeFilter.js; either implementation leaves $nor unvisited only if the check lives where $nor is never recursed, which is the reading used here.
